title: Exact restriction and K-flat complexes on a localized ringed site
statement: Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, and let $U$ be an object of $C$. Write $R_U=R|_U$ for the restricted ring on $C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Restriction $G\mapsto G|_U$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is exact. For every possibly unbounded cochain complex $K^\bullet$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], if $K^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], then its termwise restriction $K^\bullet|_U$ is K-flat over $R_U$. There is no assumption that the terms of $K^\bullet$ are flat.

proof.text: Write $j^*G=G|_U$ and $L=j_{U!}$ for the sheafified direct-sum extension by zero. By lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, $j^*$ is exact and $L$ is an exact (in particular additive) left adjoint to $j^*$. This proves the exactness assertion of the item. The ring on the slice is exactly $R_U=R|_U$, so this is restriction of modules over the ring specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site; Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; restriction exactness also used in Tag 0E8G, lemma-j-shriek-reflects-exactness.

proof.text: Let G be an arbitrary acyclic complex on the slice. The additive exact extension L preserves exactness of each short complex, by the Mathlib exact-functor API. Thus LG is acyclic. Apply the defining K-flatness of K to LG to obtain acyclicity of Tot(LG tensor K).

source.place: Tag 0E8K, lemma-restriction-K-flat, first sentence and first displayed total tensor; Definition 06YN, definition-K-flat.

proof.text: For a small family $(M_i)$ of $R_U$-modules, $L$ commutes with its direct sum. Indeed for every $R$-module $H$ the adjunction gives natural bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_R(L(\bigoplus_i M_i),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_U}(\bigoplus_i M_i,j^*H)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{R_U}(M_i,j^*H)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(LM_i,H).$$ Thus $L(\bigoplus_i M_i)$ with the maps $L\iota_i$ has the coproduct universal property, and the canonical map $\bigoplus_i LM_i\to L(\bigoplus_i M_i)$ is an isomorphism. The module direct sums used here exist as in def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves; in the application their index set is $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$, small in the coefficient universe.

source.place: Tag 0E8K, lemma-restriction-K-flat, proof: j_{U!} commutes with direct sums as a left adjoint; the Hom argument spells out that observation.

proof.text: Put $A^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(G^\bullet\otimes_{R_U}K^\bullet|_U)$. For each degree $n$, step 3 followed by the natural tensor isomorphisms of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor gives $$\theta^n:L(A^n)=L(\bigoplus_{p+q=n}G^p\otimes_{R_U}K^q|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{p+q=n}L(G^p\otimes_{R_U}K^q|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{p+q=n}LG^p\otimes_R K^q=T^n.$$ These are maps of complexes: on the $(p,q)$ summand, naturality in $G^p$ identifies the component $L(d_G^p\otimes 1)$ with $L(d_G^p)\otimes 1$, and naturality in $K^q$ identifies $L(1\otimes d_K^q|_U)$ with $1\otimes d_K^q$. The coproduct comparison respects its injections. Additivity of $L$ from step 1 respects the sum of these two components and the coefficient $(-1)^p$ of the second. These are precisely the signed differentials defining both total complexes, so $\theta:LA^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}T^\bullet$ is a complex isomorphism. All sums are direct sums, including for unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 0E8K, lemma-restriction-K-flat, displayed equality of total complexes and its justification; uses Modules on Sites Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor.

proof.text: The extension L is faithful: evaluate equality of extended maps on the summand indexed by the structure arrow X to U. Equality after sheafification gives local equality by local injectivity of the unit. Projection to that summand gives local equality of the original maps, hence equality by sheaf separatedness. An additive exact faithful functor between abelian categories reflects exactness (Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_map_iff_of_faithful). Apply this to each short complex of Tot(G tensor K|U), whose extension is acyclic by the signed total-complex isomorphism. Thus the original total complex is acyclic. Quantification over all acyclic G is precisely K-flatness of the restriction; no boundedness or termwise flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 0E8K, lemma-restriction-K-flat, final sentence; Modules on Sites Tag 0E8G, lemma-j-shriek-reflects-exactness.
